title: OpenAI's new chip Jalapeño beats Nvidia, leads SemiAnalysis's power comparison - TCR 08/26/26
description:
OpenAI's first custom chip Jalapeño outperformed every Nvidia, AMD, and Google part included in SemiAnalysis's comparison on tokens-per-watt in what OpenAI says was about 16 months from design start to working silicon, Bill Gates reversed his 2023 AI-jobs stance and called for a compute tax, and Global Energy Monitor counted 189 gigawatts of gas capacity planned to power US data centers.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-august-26-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
1:02 OpenAI's Jalapeño beats Nvidia on power
4:28 Bill Gates reverses on AI jobs
7:13 Data-center backlash hardens into rules
10:02 SpaceX's $100 billion Louisiana spaceport
12:56 A designed antibody meets Ebola's deadliest strain
15:42 Close

This episode covers the Jalapeño comparison using figures supplied in part by OpenAI and the "CUDA moat" question, the open-sourced AgentX benchmark, Bill Gates on token taxes and human-only work, the 189 GW gas buildout racing Australian siting rules, SpaceX's plan to spend up to $100 billion on the Starbase Louisiana spaceport on contested wetlands, and the first human use of the MBP134 antibody cocktail against Ebola's Bundibugyo strain.

The through-line is the binding constraint on machine intelligence sliding from chips to power, so every story orbits the watt. SemiAnalysis published the first outside data on OpenAI's Jalapeño chip, which won on throughput-per-watt against every Nvidia, AMD, and Google part included in the comparison on the open models tested, and called the CUDA lock-in "potentially dead" - the AgentX benchmark used in the comparison is now open for labs and buyers with compatible hardware and software to run. Bill Gates walked back his "manageable transition" framing, warning of far fewer jobs and proposing a compute tax to fund a broad floor plus categories of work reserved for humans. On the cost side, 189 gigawatts of gas capacity is planned as reports say developers are filing permits in hopes of being grandfathered past proposed siting rules, Foxglove says two UK campuses could exceed ExxonMobil's reported UK emissions footprint in 2023, and SpaceX announced plans to spend up to $100 billion on a 125,000-acre Louisiana spaceport on subsiding marsh next to two wildlife refuges. And in the deadliest filovirus outbreak ever recorded, a designed pan-Ebolavirus antibody cocktail cured an infected health worker and shielded four exposed children, closing the gap between a designed molecule and a fielded defense inside the emergency.
